title: Cross-layer SLO fusion and adaptive pager windows for low-signal endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a cross-layer SLO fusion pipeline that combines trace-derived signatures, metrics distributions, and log-derived error markers into a single composite SLO signal for low-traffic endpoints. Introduce adaptive pager windows that expand/contract based on baseline noise and recent anomaly confidence to reduce false pages for sparse services while preserving fast response for true degradations.
acceptance_criteria: Composite SLO signal computed in prod for at least three low-traffic routes with documented baseline behavior
Adaptive pager window implemented in paging policy service with configurable min/max window sizes
Burn-rate alerting rules updated to consult composite SLO and anomaly confidence score before paging
Dashboards show before/after alert volume and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for target routes
Integration test that injects synthetic trace spikes, metrics drift, and log error bursts to validate expected pager behavior
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ava Chen: Kickoff — scoped work to three candidate endpoints: /embeddings/submit, /runtime/generate-stream, and /batch/annotate. Chosen for mixed traffic patterns and recent noisy alerts.
2026-02-14 - Mateo Rivera: Prototype trace hook enrichment — added route and model metadata tags (route_id, model_family, quant_profile) to span root. Minimal overhead observed in canary cluster.
2026-02-18 - Priya Patel (SRE): Review feedback — prefer storing anomaly confidence as discrete tiers (low/medium/high) to simplify pager rules. Also requested opt-in rollout per team.
2026-02-22 - Mateo Rivera: Metrics pipeline change — added per-route percentile sketch (tdigest) in metrics-ingest to keep memory bounded; emits p50/p90/p99 and distribution entropy every minute.
2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Decided composite SLO will weight signals: traces(40%), metrics(40%), logs(20%). We will tune weights post-rollout based on precision/recall on historical incidents.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Lina Ortiz): Dashboard mockups approved; need explicit signal breakdown to help oncall understand composite failures.
2026-03-06 - Mateo Rivera: Implemented adaptive window algorithm in paging-policy-service: base_window=5m, max_window=30m, scale factor based on rolling entropy and anomaly tier. Unit tests added.

2026-03-10 - QA: Ran synthetic injection test against canary routes. Observed 72% reduction in false pages for noise-only scenarios; slight increase in time-to-page for very short high-severity spikes — investigating threshold tuning.
2026-03-12 - PM feedback (Zara Ahmed): Schedule a 48-hour dark-launch for one internal team and collect MTTA and oncall survey before broader rollout. Add metrics to monitor missed true positives.
Follow-ups: Add Opt-Out tag for teams; add playbook entries for triage of composite SLO alerts.
runbook: Create composite SLO alert -> check anomaly tier on alert metadata -> if tier==high or composite_score>0.8 then page immediately; if tier==medium then widen pager window and re-evaluate after window; if tier==low then create ticket and notify triage channel only.
notes: Key trade-offs: fusion reduces noisy pages for sparse routes but adds complexity to RCA because multiple signals can mask a single causal change. Will instrument signal provenance and provide a one-click expand view in the dashboard to show individual trace/metric/log contributions.
